name: Flavor of the Month Scholarship
description: Inspired by National Ice Cream Month, this scholarship asks applicants to describe which ice cream flavor they would be and why. It is a fun, short-essay scholarship open to students of all ages throughout the United States.
requirements: Answer a short essay question comparing yourself to an ice cream flavor.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Make Me Laugh Scholarship
description: A fun scholarship that invites applicants to share a genuinely funny or embarrassing story to make the committee laugh. It is designed to give students a break from traditional scholarship applications.
requirements: Submit a humorous short essay or story that generates a real laugh.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Shout It Out Scholarship
description: This scholarship encourages students to express whatever is on their mind, whether a message for the world or a personal thought, in a short essay. It rewards students for speaking up and sharing their voice.
requirements: Answer a short essay question sharing what is on your mind.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Zombie Apocalypse Scholarship
description: This scholarship asks applicants to describe their zombie survival plan in a short essay, inspired by post-apocalyptic scenarios. It is a creative and imaginative scholarship open to students nationwide.
requirements: Submit a short essay describing your zombie apocalypse survival plan.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Education Matters Scholarship
description: This scholarship asks applicants to respond to naysayers who argue that college is not worth it, making the case for the value of education. It is aimed at students who are passionate about the importance of higher education.
requirements: Submit a short essay addressing why education matters in response to those who argue against college.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Top Ten List Scholarship
description: Rather than limiting applicants to just one thing about themselves, this scholarship invites students to share a top ten list of what they want people to know about them. It celebrates the multifaceted nature of each applicant.
requirements: Submit a top ten list describing what you want people to know about you.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Unigo $10K Scholarship
description: Unigo's largest scholarship award of $10,000 is available to students throughout the United States. Applicants complete a short essay question for a chance to win this significant college funding award.
requirements: Answer a short essay question as part of the application.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: I Have a Dream Scholarship
description: This scholarship invites students to share a dream they have had and reflect on how dreams can shape ideas, perceptions, and educational goals. It is a creative short-essay scholarship open to students nationwide.
requirements: Submit a short essay about a dream you have had and its impact on your life or education.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Sweet and Simple Scholarship
description: Applicants are asked to reflect on a simple yet meaningful gift or gesture that made a strong impact on their life. This scholarship celebrates the power of humble and unassuming moments.
requirements: Submit a short essay describing a simple gift or gesture that had a meaningful impact on your life.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Superpower Scholarship
description: This scholarship asks students to imagine having a superpower and describe what they would do with it. It is a creative, fun scholarship designed for hero lovers and imaginative thinkers.
requirements: Submit a short essay about what superpower you would choose and how you would use it.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: All About Education Scholarship
description: Inspired by the saying 'education is the key to success,' this scholarship asks students to reflect on what doors their education could open for them. It is aimed at college-bound students who value the transformative power of a degree.
requirements: Submit a short essay about what opportunities your education could unlock.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Fifth Month Scholarship
description: This scholarship celebrates the number five and invites students to reflect on its significance in a short essay. It is a lighthearted and creative scholarship open to students throughout the United States.
requirements: Submit a short essay about the significance of the number five.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: Do-Over Scholarship
description: This scholarship asks applicants to reflect on a moment in their life they would choose to do over and how that change would affect their future. It encourages thoughtful self-reflection through a short essay.
requirements: Submit a short essay describing a moment in your life you would do over and why.
eligibility: Students ages 14 and up in the United States

name: 2026-2027 MetLife Foundation Legacy Endowed Scholarship
description: The MetLife Foundation Legacy Endowed Scholarship is offered through UNCF as part of its scholarship of the month feature. It supports high-achieving minority students pursuing college degrees.

name: Health Care Scholars United
description: Health Care Scholars United supports 30 high-achieving students committed to pursuing a clinical professional career. The program provides renewable merit-based scholarships, wrap-around scholar support services, and exam/licensure prep and registration fee stipends.
requirements: Must be committed to pursuing a clinical professional career; must complete all steps of the application including all information and essays
eligibility: High-achieving students committed to a clinical professional career

name: Fund II Foundation UNCF STEM Scholars Program
description: A scholarship program managed by UNCF supporting students in STEM fields. It is one of several specialty scholarship programs administered by UNCF for minority students.
requirements: Must meet UNCF eligibility criteria; must complete all application steps including required essays
eligibility: Minority students attending UNCF-affiliated or partner schools

name: UNCF/Koch Scholars Program
description: A scholarship program managed by UNCF in partnership with Koch providing support to minority students. It comes with its own eligibility criteria, application requirements, and deadlines.
requirements: Must meet UNCF and Koch eligibility criteria; must complete all application steps including required essays
eligibility: Minority students attending UNCF-affiliated or partner schools

name: K-12 Education Fellowship
description: A fellowship program managed by UNCF supporting students or educators focused on K-12 education. It comes with its own eligibility criteria, application requirements, and deadlines.
requirements: Must meet UNCF eligibility criteria; must complete all application steps including required essays
eligibility: Students or educators focused on K-12 education

name: Frederick Douglass Bicentennial Scholarship Program
description: A scholarship program managed by UNCF honoring Frederick Douglass and supporting minority students in their pursuit of college degrees. It comes with its own eligibility criteria, application requirements, and deadlines.
requirements: Must meet UNCF eligibility criteria; must complete all application steps including required essays
eligibility: Minority students attending UNCF-affiliated or partner schools

name: ScholarshipOwl No Essay Scholarship
description: A no-essay scholarship open to students seeking free money for college. Applicants simply enter for a chance to win a large cash award without writing an essay.
requirements: No essay required
eligibility: College students

name: Niche $10,000 "No Essay" Scholarship
description: A no-essay scholarship offering $10,000 to a lucky winner. Students can enter quickly without writing an essay for a chance to win free money for college.
requirements: No essay required
eligibility: College students

name: "Be Bold" No Essay Scholarship
description: A no-essay scholarship awarding $25,000 to a selected student. Applicants can enter without writing an essay for a chance to win free money for college.
requirements: No essay required
eligibility: College students

name: Sallie $2,000 Scholarship
description: A fast and easy $2,000 scholarship entry requiring no essay. Applicants provide basic personal information for a chance to win free money for college.
requirements: No essay required; provide basic personal information
eligibility: College students

name: Most Valuable Student Scholarship - First Place
description: The Most Valuable Student Scholarship is awarded to current high school seniors who are U.S. citizens, judged on scholarship, leadership, and financial need. The Top 20 scholars selected from 500 national semi-finalists receive a $30,000 four-year award and an invitation to the MVS Leadership Weekend. Attendance at Leadership Weekend is required to receive the First Place award.
requirements: Applicants must be current high school seniors (or equivalent) and U.S. citizens at the time of application. High school graduates are not eligible. Must enroll in a four-year undergraduate degree program at an accredited U.S. college or university. Judged on scholarship, leadership, and financial need.
eligibility: Current high school seniors or equivalent who are U.S. citizens; no relation to an Elks member required; permanent legal resident status does not qualify

name: Most Valuable Student Scholarship - Runners Up
description: The Most Valuable Student Scholarship runners-up award is granted to 480 students who qualify as national semi-finalists but are not selected among the Top 20. Recipients receive a $4,000 four-year scholarship for undergraduate study at an accredited U.S. college or university. Applicants are judged on scholarship, leadership, and financial need.
requirements: Applicants must be current high school seniors (or equivalent) and U.S. citizens at the time of application. High school graduates are not eligible. Must enroll in a four-year undergraduate degree program at an accredited U.S. college or university. Judged on scholarship, leadership, and financial need.
eligibility: Current high school seniors or equivalent who are U.S. citizens; no relation to an Elks member required; permanent legal resident status does not qualify

name: Demo Scholarship Program
description: A scholarship program established by Demo Sponsor to assist children of employees who plan to continue their education in college or vocational school programs. Awards are granted without regard to race, color, creed, religion, sexual orientation, age, gender, disability, or national origin. The program is administered by Scholarship America.
requirements: Applicants must be an eligible Demo Sponsor unit associate, be high school graduates or current postsecondary undergraduate or graduate level students, and plan to enroll in full-time or part-time undergraduate or graduate study at an accredited two-year or four-year college, university or vocational-technical school. Evaluated on academic information, leadership and participation in school and community activities, work experience, and financial need. Special consideration given to first-generation students.
eligibility: Children of eligible Demo Sponsor unit associates who are high school graduates or current undergraduate or graduate students; must plan to enroll in accredited two-year or four-year college, university, or vocational-technical school

name: Power Poetry Scholarship Slam
description: This poetry contest is available for young poets in the United States who submit an original poem on the current scholarship slam topic. Power Poetry is an online poetry community founded on the belief that words and poems can have the power to change the world.
requirements: Submit an original poem on the current scholarship slam topic.
eligibility: Young poets in the United States.

name: Jameela Jamil x I Weigh Scholarship
description: I Weigh is all about radical inclusivity and allyship, creating a community where no one feels alone. This scholarship aims to amplify voices and advocate for individuals to share their stories with the world. The mission is to inspire learning and growth both individually and collectively.
requirements: Submit your story or voice to be heard by the world; commitment to radical inclusivity and allyship.
eligibility: Open to applicants who want to share their story and voice.

name: Keep Going Forward No Essay Scholarship
description: This scholarship exists to support anyone moving on to somewhere or something new in life, whether that is a new town, new school, new passion, or new phase of life. It is open to all students and non-students in any stage of life or field of study. The only requirement is that you are moving forward toward something new.
requirements: Must be moving forward toward something new in life; no essay required.
eligibility: Open to all students and non-students in any stage of life.

name: The LSAT Prep Courses Scholarship
description: Law school scholarships offered to support students pursuing legal education. Awards may be based on merit, including undergraduate performance, work experience, or LSAT scores, as well as financial need. Twelve awards are offered annually.
requirements: May be merit-based (undergraduate performance, work, or LSAT scores) or need-based (demonstrated financial need).
eligibility: Law school students or prospective law school students.

name: grownish broke- Student Loan Payoff
description: This scholarship is aimed at helping current undergraduate or graduate students or alumni with student loan payoff. Applicants must be US residents over 18 years of age. Three awards are available totaling $450,000.
requirements: Must be a US resident, over 18 years of age, and a current undergraduate or graduate student or alumni.
eligibility: US residents, age 18+, current undergraduate or graduate students or alumni.

name: City of Houston Public Service Recognition Week Scholarship Essay Contest
description: High school seniors can earn up to $2,000 for college while gaining a deeper understanding about local government and learning about career options serving Houston residents. Five awards totaling $50,000 are available.
requirements: Must be a high school senior; submit an essay related to public service and local government.
eligibility: High school seniors in Houston, Texas.

name: Goldberg Osborne Arizona Don't Text Drive Scholarship
description: This scholarship is open to Arizona students who are currently attending a college or trade school or who plan to attend for fall 2020. Students must pledge to not text and drive. Twelve awards totaling $12,000 are offered.
requirements: Must pledge to not text and drive; must be attending or planning to attend a college or trade school.
eligibility: Arizona students currently attending or planning to attend college or trade school.

name: Countdown to College Scholarship
description: This award is available for U.S. students who are in grades 9-12. Students must sign up for Potential Magazine's weekly email newsletter to be considered. One award of $1,000 is available.
requirements: Must sign up for Potential Magazine's weekly email newsletter.
eligibility: U.S. students in grades 9-12.

name: Win Free College Tuition Sweepstakes
description: All students who register on NextStepU.com during an eligible drawing period and opt in to Win Free Tuition will qualify for this sweepstakes. One award of $2,500 is available.
requirements: Must register on NextStepU.com during an eligible drawing period and opt in to Win Free Tuition.
eligibility: All students who register on NextStepU.com.

name: Sallie Mae Plan for College Sweepstakes
description: The Sallie Mae Plan for College Sweepstakes is available for U.S. students who are 18 years of age or older. Applicants must register an account with Sallie Mae and fill out an application form. One award of $1,000 is offered annually.
requirements: Must register an account with Sallie Mae and fill out an application form.
eligibility: U.S. students aged 18 or older.
